propositions: Plans assert false capability-surface claims about named modules (module exists but specific capability is absent, or capability is present when plan asserts it must be built), causing the executing agent to rely on non-existent capabilities or redundantly rebuild existing ones.

The existing E4 criterion misses capability-surface mismatches because it only validates module existence, not the finer-grained capability surface (as demonstrated by three verified misses: dc58 with signing location, db7b with compaction scope, 5886 with duplicate alert emission).

A new advisory, code-grounded, agent-tier criterion named 'asserted-capability' must be added to the G6/E4 rubric family in the codebase-grounding facet to fire on symmetric capability assertions: either (A) plan asserts module provides capability but code lacks it, or (B) plan asserts capability is absent but code provides it.

The criterion must be registered as advisory (never blocking) in registry.CANONICAL_LLM, CODEBASE_GROUNDED, and AGENT_TIER; routed in criteria_routing.json with exec=AGENT and facet=codebase-grounding; and documented via rubric prompt and regenerated guide section to pass validation checks.

The bounded sanity check must demonstrate the probe fires on at least 2 of 3 verified-miss cases (dc58, db7b, 5886) and records any clean-plan fires as advisory (non-blocking) dogfood datapoints for the advisory-to-blocking promotion gate.
The criterion must auto-integrate into the standing effectiveness recorder with zero per-criterion wiring, recording detection and false-accept signals for future dogfood-gated promotion.
